newsitem.title: USA: AT&T sees no role for Telefonica in Unisource.
newsitem.headline: AT&T sees no role for Telefonica in Unisource.

text.p: AT&T Corp said Telefonica de Espana SA's strategic pact with the rival Concert alliance is "incompatible" with Telefonica's membership in the AT&T-backed Unisource NV telecoms alliance.
An AT&T spokeswoman said that, "AT&T stands with its partners in Unisource in believing that Telefonica's link with BT/MCI is incompatible with its shareholding in Unisource."

Earlier Friday, AT&T's partners in the pan-European Unisource alliance had called on Telefonica to leave in light of its pact with Concert, the British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp group.
Unisource shareholders include Koninklijke PTT Nederland, the Dutch national phone company, Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT.
In a statement, the U.S. telephone giant said it regrets Telefonica's decision "to pursue their own interests at the expense of their partnership with AT&T and Unisource."
AT&T said it remains committed to Unisource, and to the companies' continued cooperation in Europe.

"AT&T-Unisource is the best option for customers and service innovation in Europe and we will do everything in our power to assure its continued success," said John Walter, AT&T's president and chief operating officer, said.
